DISTRICT OF MARSHFIELD PUBLIC SCHOOLS

**District Accessibility Plan 2025**

**Approval and Effective Date**

This District Accessibility Plan 2025 (the "Plan") is approved and adopted by the Facilities & Operations Division, in coordination with the Office of Student Services and the Office of Civil Rights Compliance. The Accessibility Plan 2025 approval date is 2025-06-10, as recorded in the plan. Record status: current. This Plan is effective as of June 10, 2025, and supersedes all prior revisions, including Rev. 2.1 (dated November 2024) and Rev. 2.0 (dated April 2024).

Director, Facilities & Operations

**1. Purpose**

This Plan establishes district-wide accessibility standards and priorities for all school facilities, administrative buildings, and outdoor instructional areas. It governs all accessibility modifications, including new construction, renovation, and interim corrective actions. Contractors, architects, and district staff shall conform to the standards herein unless a specific project is governed by a more restrictive federal, state, or local code requirement, in which case the more restrictive requirement shall apply.

**2. Scope**

This Plan applies to all facilities owned or leased by the district, including but not limited to:
- Elementary, middle, and high school buildings
- Administrative offices
- Maintenance and transportation facilities
- Playgrounds, athletic fields, and associated structures
- Temporary classrooms and portable units

**3. Standards and Priorities**

The following sections establish minimum accessibility standards. Priorities are assigned as P1 (high), P2 (medium), and P3 (lower) to guide sequencing of work. P1 items shall be addressed in the current fiscal year; P2 items shall be scheduled within two years; P3 items shall be included in the capital improvements plan.

**3.1 Doorways and Entrances**

| Item | Standard | Priority |
|------|----------|----------|
| Clear width of all primary entrance doors | 32 inches minimum, measured from face of door to opposite stop | P1 |
| Clear width of interior doors serving classrooms, restrooms, and offices | 32 inches minimum; 36 inches preferred for new construction | P1 |
| Threshold height at exterior doors | 1/2 inch maximum, beveled | P1 |
| Door hardware | Operable with one hand, no tight grasping or twisting; lever-style preferred | P1 |
| Force to open interior doors | 5.0 lbf maximum | P2 |
| Maneuvering clearance at doors | Per ANSI A117.1-2017, Section 404 | P2 |

**3.2 Restrooms**

| Item | Standard | Priority |
|------|----------|----------|
| Accessible stall clear floor space | 60 inches wide x 60 inches deep, with door swinging outward | P1 |
| Grab bar diameter | 1.25 to 1.5 inches, with 1.5 inch clearance from wall | P1 |
| Toilet seat height | 17 to 19 inches | P1 |
| Sink height (knee clearance) | 27 inches minimum knee clearance, 30 inches minimum toe clearance | P2 |
| Faucet controls | Lever, push-button, or sensor operated; operable with one hand | P2 |

**3.3 Signage**

| Item | Standard | Priority |
|------|----------|----------|
| Permanent room identification signs | Raised characters and Braille; mounted 48 to 60 inches above floor | P1 |
| Directional signage to accessible routes | Provided at inaccessible building entrances | P1 |
| Sign contrast | 70% contrast minimum between characters and background | P2 |

**3.4 Parking**

| Item | Standard | Priority |
|------|----------|----------|
| Accessible parking space width | 96 inches minimum; van-accessible spaces 132 inches minimum | P1 |
| Access aisle width | 60 inches minimum for car spaces; 60 inches for van spaces | P1 |
| Slope of parking space and aisle | 1:48 maximum in all directions | P2 |
| Number of accessible spaces | Per Table 208.2 of the 2010 ADA Standards | P1 |
**4. IMPLEMENTATION SCHEDULE**

**4.1 Phased Work Plan**

The district will implement the accessibility improvements identified in Section 3 over a three-year cycle, with the highest-priority items (P1) completed by the end of the 2025-2026 school year. P2 items will be scheduled as funding allows, with a target completion date of June 30, 2028. The table below reflects the approved phasing as of the June 10, 2025 revision.

| Phase | Timeframe | Scope | Funding Source |

DISTRICT OF MARSHFIELD PUBLIC SCHOOLS
Facilities & Operations Division
**District Accessibility Plan 2025**
Rev. 3.0

**Approval and Effective Date**

This District Accessibility Plan 2025 (the "Plan") is approved and adopted by the Facilities & Operations Division, in coordination with the Office of Student Services and the Office of Civil Rights Compliance. The Accessibility Plan 2025 approval date is 2025-06-10, as recorded in the plan. Record status: current. This Plan is effective as of June 10, 2025, and supersedes all prior revisions, including Rev. 2.1 (dated November 2024) and Rev. 2.0 (dated April 2024).

Approved by:

_________________________
Diane M. Kowalski
Director, Facilities & Operations
Date: June 10, 2025

_________________________
Rev. Marcus T. Ellison
Superintendent of Schools
Date: June 10, 2025

---

**1. Purpose**

This Plan establishes district-wide accessibility standards and priorities for all school facilities, administrative buildings, and outdoor instructional areas. It governs all accessibility modifications, including new construction, renovation, and interim corrective actions. Contractors, architects, and district staff shall conform to the standards herein unless a specific project is governed by a more restrictive federal, state, or local code requirement, in which case the more restrictive requirement shall apply.

**2. Scope**

This Plan applies to all facilities owned or leased by the district, including but not limited to:
- Elementary, middle, and high school buildings
- Administrative offices
- Maintenance and transportation facilities
- Playgrounds, athletic fields, and associated structures
- Temporary classrooms and portable units

**3. Standards and Priorities**

The following sections establish minimum accessibility standards. Priorities are assigned as P1 (high), P2 (medium), and P3 (lower) to guide sequencing of work. P1 items shall be addressed in the current fiscal year; P2 items shall be scheduled within two years; P3 items shall be included in the capital improvements plan.

**3.1 Doorways and Entrances**

| Item | Standard | Priority |
|------|----------|----------|
| Clear width of all primary entrance doors | 32 inches minimum, measured from face of door to opposite stop | P1 |
| Clear width of interior doors serving classrooms, restrooms, and offices | 32 inches minimum; 36 inches preferred for new construction | P1 |
| Threshold height at exterior doors | 1/2 inch maximum, beveled | P1 |
| Door hardware | Operable with one hand, no tight grasping or twisting; lever-style preferred | P1 |
| Force to open interior doors | 5.0 lbf maximum | P2 |
| Maneuvering clearance at doors | Per ANSI A117.1-2017, Section 404 | P2 |

**3.2 Restrooms**

| Item | Standard | Priority |
|------|----------|----------|
| Accessible stall clear floor space | 60 inches wide x 60 inches deep, with door swinging outward | P1 |
| Grab bar diameter | 1.25 to 1.5 inches, with 1.5 inch clearance from wall | P1 |
| Toilet seat height | 17 to 19 inches | P1 |
| Sink height (knee clearance) | 27 inches minimum knee clearance, 30 inches minimum toe clearance | P2 |
| Faucet controls | Lever, push-button, or sensor operated; operable with one hand | P2 |

**3.3 Signage**

| Item | Standard | Priority |
|------|----------|----------|
| Permanent room identification signs | Raised characters and Braille; mounted 48 to 60 inches above floor | P1 |
| Directional signage to accessible routes | Provided at inaccessible building entrances | P1 |
| Sign contrast | 70% contrast minimum between characters and background | P2 |

**3.4 Parking**

| Item | Standard | Priority |
|------|----------|----------|
| Accessible parking space width | 96 inches minimum; van-accessible spaces 132 inches minimum | P1 |
| Access aisle width | 60 inches minimum for car spaces; 60 inches for van spaces | P1 |
| Slope of parking space and aisle | 1:48 maximum in all directions | P2 |
| Number of accessible spaces | Per Table 208.2 of the 2010 ADA Standards | P1 |

**4. IMPLEMENTATION SCHEDULE**

**4.1 Phased Work Plan**

The district will implement the accessibility improvements identified in Section 3 over a three-year cycle, with the highest-priority items (P1) completed by the end of the 2025-2026 school year. P2 items will be scheduled as funding allows, with a target completion date of June 30, 2028. The table below reflects the approved phasing as of the June 10, 2025 revision.

| Phase | Timeframe | Scope | Funding Source |
|-------|-----------|-------|----------------|
| Phase 1 | July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2026 | All P1 items: doorways, restrooms, signage, parking, and route-of-travel corrections at all schools | Capital Improvements Fund, Bond 2024 |
| Phase 2 | July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027 | P2 items at elementary schools; begin interior door hardware replacement at middle schools | Capital Improvements Fund, State ADA Grant |
| Phase 3 | July 1, 2027 – June 30, 2028 | Remaining P2 items; verification and closeout inspections | Capital Improvements Fund |

Work orders for Phase 1 were issued on May 15, 2025, and construction is scheduled to begin at all sites no later than July 7, 2025. The Facilities Department will issue a monthly progress report to the Superintendent’s Cabinet, with the first report due August 1, 2025.

**4.2 Site-by-Site Schedule**

The following schedule identifies the start and completion dates for each school. Dates are subject to change if weather or permit delays occur; the Facilities Director will communicate any changes in writing no later than five business days before the affected date.

Door ID: LIB-D1 (active leaf) / LIB-D2 (inactive leaf)

DESCRIPTION OF WORK:
Adjust the Library Entrance door set to ensure proper closing and clearance. The active leaf (LIB-D1) is currently binding at the threshold and does not fully latch when closed. The door also appears to rub against the frame on the latch side, which has worn a groove in the paint and may be affecting the weather seal.

Specific items to address:
1. Check and adjust the closing speed and latch speed on the closer for LIB-D1. Door currently closes too fast in the final 30 degrees, causing the latch to strike the strike plate instead of sliding in.
2. Verify hinge alignment on both leaves. Top hinge on LIB-D1 appears loose; screws may need to be replaced with longer anchors if the wood is stripped.
3. Confirm that the threshold is not the cause of the binding. If the threshold is raised or damaged, repair or replace as needed.
4. Check the door width measurement against the current accessibility plan. The Library Entrance door width measurement is 36.0 inches, noted during inspection. Record status: current. This measurement is the current clearance for the active leaf with the door open 90 degrees. Do not reduce this clearance during adjustment.
5. Inspect the sweep on the bottom of LIB-D1. Sweep is dragging on the threshold and may need to be trimmed or replaced.
6. Verify that the inactive leaf (LIB-D2) is properly secured with the manual flush bolts and that the header bolt engages fully.

NOTES:
- The door set was previously adjusted in March 2025 (see WO-2025-0187). That work order noted a similar binding issue, but the problem has returned. The closer may be undersized for the door weight, or the frame may be out of square. Contractor should evaluate whether a new closer is needed rather than another adjustment.
